description: Stonewright prompt library: outcome-oriented starters for MCP clients. Prefer stonewright-task-start; do not paste full prompts into task-start responses.

prompts.title: Inspect site snapshot
prompts.summary: Capture a compact operational overview before changing anything.
prerequisites: Signed in with OAuth or an Application Password
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright on this WordPress site. Call stonewright-task-start first. Then run stonewright-site-snapshot and stonewright-content-inventory. Summarize name, theme, plugin counts, post counts, mode, MCP surface, and the top content types. Do not mutate the site.
prompts.verification: Response includes mode, mcp_surface, and at least post/page counts without write tools.

prompts.title: Repair from site pulse
prompts.summary: Score hardening/performance and apply the top safe fixes.
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Start with stonewright-task-start, then stonewright-site-pulse. For each failed high/critical check, propose a concrete repair. Apply only reversible fixes through typed abilities (stonewright-settings-update, stonewright-wp-cli-run), then confirm each one with stonewright-site-health-test. Confirm mode first and skip production-safe destructive steps without tokens. If a write returns a Rescue error or a pending_incident, stop and call stonewright-rescue-status. Do not use stonewright-php-execute for routine pulse repairs.
prompts.verification: Pulse score and fixes list present; any writes audited and each fix confirmed by a health test; no confirmation_token skipped in production-safe; no write continued after a Rescue error.

prompts.title: Repair a failed change and keep the lineage
prompts.summary: Fix a write that failed verification, link the repair to it, and see the chain in the Audit log.
prerequisites: The change_set_id of the failed write (in its result or error data)
An Elementor V3 or Gutenberg page
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start. A write on page {{post_id}} failed verification. Take its change_set_id from the result or the error data and read what the change set lists as missing or unexpected. Fix only that cause with one dry run and one apply of stonewright-elementor-v3-batch-mutate (or stonewright-blocks-batch-mutate on a block page), passing repair_of set to that change_set_id. For Elementor, run stonewright-elementor-css-regenerate, then stonewright-elementor-post-write-verify with the change_set the repair returned. Report whether its verification is verified. Make no unrelated change. Tell me the chain (the failed change, its failed verification, the repair, verified) is shown in Stonewright > Audit log.
prompts.verification: The repair has repair_of set and its verification is verified; the earlier incident is resolved; the Audit log shows the chain.

prompts.title: Restore a page to an earlier snapshot
prompts.summary: List the Stonewright snapshots of a page and restore the one I pick.
prerequisites: A snapshot exists (every Stonewright write to a post takes one)
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start, then stonewright-change-log with post_id {{post_id}} to list its snapshots. Show me the candidates with their times and wait for my pick. Restore the chosen snapshot with stonewright-change-restore (post_id and snapshot_id; in production-safe mode also a confirmation_token from stonewright-security-issue-confirmation-token for exactly those arguments). The restore snapshots the current state first, so it can be undone. Then read the page back and verify desktop and mobile.
prompts.verification: The chosen snapshot_id is restored with restored:true; a new snapshot of the state before the restore exists; the page renders at desktop and mobile.

prompts.title: Elementor landing page from brief
prompts.summary: Build a new Elementor landing page with native widgets first.
prerequisites: Elementor V3 page (classic widgets and containers)
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start. Plan with stonewright-design-native-plan, then validate the DesignSpec with stonewright-design-validate-spec. Build with stonewright-elementor-v3-build-page-from-spec: dry_run:true first, then one apply once the diagnostics are clean (the apply snapshots the page). Polish with stonewright-elementor-v3-batch-mutate. Prefer native Elementor widgets. Then run stonewright-elementor-css-regenerate for the page and stonewright-elementor-post-write-verify with the touched element ids, and verify desktop/tablet/mobile in a separate tab with no horizontal overflow.
prompts.verification: Page has Elementor data; digest shows structure; post-write verification passes; no raw HTML widget dump for core sections.

prompts.title: Elementor section refactor
prompts.summary: Refactor one hero/section with backup and batch mutate.
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright on page {{post_id}}. Start with stonewright-task-start, read stonewright-elementor-page-digest, and snapshot with stonewright-elementor-v3-backup-page. Change only the hero section with stonewright-elementor-v3-batch-mutate for clearer hierarchy and spacing: one dry_run:true batch, then one apply, with settings_evidence and require_evidence:true for visual changes. Then run stonewright-elementor-css-regenerate and stonewright-elementor-post-write-verify with the touched element ids. Leave other sections untouched.
prompts.verification: Backup snapshot id recorded; only targeted elements changed (change_set verified, unexpected empty); digest before/after differs in hero only.

prompts.title: Edit an Elementor V4 page through the native bridge
prompts.summary: Plan and apply a certified Elementor ability inside Stonewright's snapshot and readback; V3 stays on Stonewright's writers.
prerequisites: Plugin mode in development or staging (V4 writes are blocked in production-safe)
Elementor V4 atomic abilities switched on in Stonewright > Setup > Settings
Elementor's own MCP module on, with an Elementor version Stonewright has certified (the capabilities report says which)
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start and stonewright-site-capabilities, and read native_elementor: its state, the Elementor version, and which abilities are certified. Only certified abilities run natively. If none is certified, say so and use Stonewright's own V4 writers (stonewright-elementor-v4-update-node); V3 pages stay on the V3 writers, and no page is ever converted. For the change on page {{post_id}}, call stonewright-elementor-native-execute with dry_run left true, show me the plan, and apply with dry_run:false only after I agree. Report the status exactly: applied, unchanged, or staged_in_autosave. A staged edit on a published page is not live; tell me, and never publish. Treat a refusal such as upstream_global_clear_cache as final and use Stonewright's own V4 class and variable writers. Verify with stonewright-elementor-post-write-verify, then desktop, tablet, and mobile.
prompts.verification: native_elementor read first; the write status is reported as applied, unchanged, or staged_in_autosave; nothing is published; the change_set verification is verified; V3 pages are untouched.

prompts.title: Gutenberg homepage hero
prompts.summary: Update a block-theme homepage hero without breaking brand tokens.
prerequisites: edit_posts capability (manage_options and edit_theme_options to write a template)
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start. Find where the homepage hero lives. On a page, read it with stonewright-blocks-parse. In a block template, list templates with stonewright-fse-list-templates and read the template with stonewright-fse-read-template. Update only the hero for a stronger headline, CTA, and mobile spacing: stonewright-blocks-batch-mutate for a page, stonewright-fse-write-template for a template (both snapshot before they write). Preserve theme.json tokens. Verify desktop and mobile.
prompts.verification: Page or template updated through one batch; theme.json tokens unchanged unless explicitly requested.

prompts.title: FSE footer cleanup
prompts.summary: Clean footer template part structure.
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Start with stonewright-task-start. Find the footer part with stonewright-fse-list-templates (type wp_template_part). Look at how it renders on the front end and in the Site Editor, then simplify its navigation and social rows for accessibility and consistent spacing, and save it with stonewright-fse-write-template-part, which snapshots the part first. Do not invent brand colors outside theme.json.
prompts.verification: Footer part saves; no horizontal overflow at 390px width.

prompts.title: Services CPT + fields
prompts.summary: Register a Services model and seed sample rows.
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start. Register a Services content type with stonewright-cpt-register (production-safe needs a confirmation token). Keep the fields for icon, headline, summary, proof metric, and CTA as post meta, or as an ACF field group with stonewright-acf-field-group-save when ACF is active. Seed six service rows with stonewright-content-bulk-upsert-posts, with each field in meta. Finish with stonewright-content-inventory to confirm counts.
prompts.verification: CPT visible in inventory; six seeded posts with their meta; REST base documented.

prompts.title: Stock image fill for hero
prompts.summary: Search Openverse/stock, import, attach alt text.
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Start with stonewright-task-start. Search stock images with stonewright-stock-image-search for the homepage hero brief, import the best licensed result with stonewright-stock-image-import, set meaningful alt text, and report the attachment id for the page builder to use.
prompts.verification: Attachment id returned; alt non-empty; license/source noted when available.

prompts.title: On-page SEO meta pass
prompts.summary: Inspect and update SEO meta for key pages.
prerequisites: Yoast SEO, Rank Math, AIOSEO, or SEOPress active
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start and stonewright-seo-status. For the homepage and top three service pages, get meta, tighten titles/descriptions to intent, update, and report before/after strings.
prompts.verification: Meta updated only on listed ids; titles ≤ ~60 chars; no keyword stuffing.

prompts.title: WP-CLI cache and rewrite health
prompts.summary: Tokenized WP-CLI status, rewrite flush when safe.
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright companion WP-CLI tools only (never shell wp). Call stonewright-task-start and stonewright-wp-cli-status, discover the rewrite and cache commands with stonewright-wp-cli-discover, then run a safe status check with stonewright-wp-cli-run. Flush rewrites only if the operator confirmed staging.
prompts.verification: All WP-CLI calls tokenized; no eval/shell; output includes command results without secrets.

prompts.title: Figma to native pixel-perfect build
prompts.summary: External Figma MCP to evidence to native plan to verify.
prerequisites: External Figma MCP tools in the client (official and/or console-bridge)
design-to-wordpress skill references/figma-mcp-extraction.md for field-to-tool map
Browser/Playwright MCP for post-write measured_targets verification
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start. List MCP tools and extract design with the client's external Figma MCP (console-bridge preferred when present: figma_export_tokens / figma_get_variables / deep component trees; official: get_variable_defs, get_design_context, get_metadata, get_screenshot). Map fields via skills/design-to-wordpress/references/figma-mcp-extraction.md. Normalize into DesignEvidence/figma_token_table (never embed Figma APIs inside Stonewright; no raw Figma tree after normalization). Call stonewright-design-native-plan. Render with the user-chosen engine (elementor|gutenberg|fse). CSS only when native_gap is recorded. Verify each breakpoint with the client's own browser tools against evidence targets (±2px spacing).
prompts.verification: Native plan present; native_gap for any CSS; no raw Figma tree after normalization; provenance set on measured values; verification notes per breakpoint.

prompts.title: Follow the active Design Direction
prompts.summary: Read the design direction the site names at connect before any visual work.
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start. The connect instructions name the active Design Direction (name, slug, id, and a contract prefix), and stonewright-task-start repeats it as design_direction_ref. If one is active, read it with stonewright-design-direction-brief before any visual work and keep to its tokens, guidance, and waivers; tell me which values you used. If none is active, tell me, say that a DESIGN.md can be imported in Stonewright > Design, and ask before inventing a style. After the work, measure the rendered page with the client's browser tools, pass the evidence to stonewright-design-quality-check, and list any place you deviated from the direction and why.
prompts.verification: The brief was read before visual work; the values used are named; quality-check findings are reported; any deviation is explained.

prompts.title: Build a page from sections my site already has
prompts.summary: Find matching sections on other pages, offer them once, copy the ones I pick, and adapt them in one batch.
prerequisites: Section reuse set to ask (Stonewright > Setup > Settings, Reuse saved sections)
A Gutenberg, Elementor V3, or Elementor V4 page (reuse never converts between builders)
Pages or saved templates you can read and edit
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start and read agent_preferences.section_reuse (the site setting stonewright_section_reuse: ask or off). If it is off, say so, tell me it can be turned on in Stonewright > Setup > Settings, and build every section from scratch. If it is ask, call stonewright-section-reuse-find with the builder (gutenberg, elementor-v3, or elementor-v4), target_post_id {{post_id}}, and the sections this page needs, for example hero, features, testimonials, contact. Ask me one short question with at most three candidates per role and their warnings, and let me pick any or none. For each pick call stonewright-section-reuse-extract, then put the copy and my text and image changes in one batch with insert_section (stonewright-elementor-v3-batch-mutate, stonewright-elementor-v4-update-node with operations, or stonewright-blocks-batch-mutate): one dry run, one apply. Follow the active Design Direction and never edit the source page. For Elementor run stonewright-elementor-css-regenerate and stonewright-elementor-post-write-verify, then verify desktop, tablet, and mobile.
prompts.verification: section_reuse read first and respected; at most one question; the change_set names a reuse_source for each copied section and its verification is verified; the source page is unchanged.

prompts.title: Upgrade tool profile mid-session
prompts.summary: When a needed tool is missing, activate a broader profile and re-list.
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start. If a required tool is missing from the list, call stonewright-tool-profile with action=activate and profile=full (or the matching specialist profile), then re-list tools (tools/list) before continuing. In Plugin mode, when the client cannot hold the full catalog, use the compact path stonewright-discover-abilities, then stonewright-get-ability-info, then stonewright-execute-ability (stonewright-php-execute stays off that profile). Do not invent shell or REST workarounds.
prompts.verification: stonewright-tool-profile returns tools_changed/re_list_instruction when applicable; subsequent tools/list includes the needed tool.

prompts.title: WooCommerce catalog inspection or guarded update
prompts.summary: Use native catalog abilities in Plugin mode or read-only store tools in Direct mode.
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright and call stonewright-task-start first. Inspect the returned mode. In Plugin mode, call stonewright-wc-status and stonewright-wc-catalog-audit, then use native wc product, variation, attribute, and term abilities with dry_run:true before any approved write; read back exact fields after apply. In Direct mode, use only stonewright-wc-products, stonewright-wc-orders, and stonewright-wc-sales-report; do not attempt catalog writes. Never change payments, checkout, taxes, or live order state unless the user explicitly expands scope.
prompts.verification: Mode reported; Plugin writes have dry-run, permission, audit, confirmation when required, and readback receipts; Direct remains read-only.

prompts.title: Direct mode safe site inspection
prompts.summary: Use the pluginless companion without degrading to ad-hoc REST or shell workarounds.
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright Direct mode. Call stonewright-task-start first, then stonewright-site-discover. Report active Direct capabilities, write mode, matched local skills, memory references, and recurring errors. Inspect content with stonewright-content-list and WooCommerce with stonewright-wc-products only through typed read tools. Do not install the plugin, use shell WP-CLI, or create REST runner scripts unless I explicitly request a mode change.
prompts.verification: stonewright-task-start reports Direct mode; no write occurs; no credential, absolute state path, or private sites.json content appears in output.

prompts.title: Look around without any write tools
prompts.summary: Switch to the read-only inspect profile: discovery, read, and verify tools only.
prerequisites: Or the operator starts the client with STONEWRIGHT_MCP_TOOL_PROFILE=inspect
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start, then stonewright-tool-profile with action=activate and profile=inspect, and re-list tools. The inspect profile keeps discovery, read, and verify tools and has no stonewright-php-execute, stonewright-execute-ability, or write tool; automatic routing never picks it. Answer my question about this site with the read tools only: {{question}}. If an answer would need a write, name the profile that owns it and ask me before switching; do not switch on your own.
prompts.verification: stonewright-tool-profile reports the inspect profile; the re-listed tools include no write tool; nothing is changed.

prompts.title: Update and verify Stonewright
prompts.summary: Match the plugin and companion versions, reload the client, and prove the live tool surface.
prompts.prompt: Help me update Stonewright without exposing credentials. Determine whether this setup uses Plugin mode, Direct mode, local stdio, or remote HTTP. Plugin mode: update the WordPress ZIP through the native updater (Stonewright > Setup > Updates). Local stdio or Direct: update the pinned companion release tarball separately. Remote HTTP: no local companion update is required. After the user restarts the MCP client, call stonewright-task-start, stonewright-ping, and stonewright-tool-profile, plus stonewright-site-info in Plugin mode or stonewright-site-discover in Direct mode. When the companion is local, also call stonewright-setup-profile, stonewright-wordpress-mcp-status, and stonewright-client-surface-check. Confirm plugin version where applicable, companion_version where applicable, expected_companion_package, startup_ready, and an empty refresh_required_tool_names list. Never inspect or print private client config.
prompts.verification: Live mode and versions match the selected release; startup_ready is true; required tool list is complete; persistent memory, skills, and audit were not reset.

prompts.title: Elementor transactional repair
prompts.summary: Batch mutate under transaction envelope with rollback.
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start. Digest the page, then stonewright-elementor-v3-transaction-run with stop_on_error and rollback_on_error. Prefer native widgets. If readback fails, confirm automatic rollback and report snapshot id. After a successful run, call stonewright-elementor-post-write-verify with the touched element ids.
prompts.verification: Transaction result ok or rolled_back with snapshot; no partial silent failure.

prompts.title: Fix my connection
prompts.summary: Diagnose MCP connection, alias, profile, and tool-surface mismatches without exposing secrets.
prerequisites: Ability to restart the MCP client
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start first. If the client cannot reach WordPress, run stonewright-ping and stonewright-site-info, then follow the Troubleshoot flow from Stonewright > Troubleshoot (sign-in addresses and connected OAuth clients are under Stonewright > Setup > Connections), or the companion connect verify/repair path for local stdio. Confirm the active alias, configured_mode, active_mode, companion_version, and that stonewright-task-start appears in tools/list after restart. If tools are truncated, call stonewright-tool-profile activate with the matching profile and re-list tools. Never print Application Passwords, OAuth tokens, or private client config.
prompts.verification: Connection mode and alias reported; stonewright-task-start visible after restart; no credentials or private config in output.

prompts.title: Build a section on my block theme
prompts.summary: Queue block changes through the block queue console instead of hand-editing serialized HTML.
prerequisites: A browser that can open the block queue console (Stonewright > Activity > Block queue)
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start. Read the target template or page with stonewright-blocks-parse, then queue one section change with stonewright-blocks-queue-change. Check stonewright-blocks-finalizer-runtime for online:true. If it is offline, give me the link from stonewright-blocks-finalizer-url (the block queue console, Stonewright > Activity > Block queue) and ask me to keep that tab open. Poll stonewright-blocks-pending-batch until the change is serialized, then persist it with stonewright-blocks-finalize-batch (it snapshots first). Preserve theme.json tokens unless I explicitly request brand changes. Verify desktop and mobile.
prompts.verification: Block queue console online; queued change finalized with readback; section renders without horizontal overflow at 390px.

prompts.title: Audit Elementor performance
prompts.summary: Measure document, settings, backup, and revision size without exposing content.
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start, then stonewright-elementor-performance-audit for page {{post_id}}. Summarize bounded size metrics, backup/revision debt, and the top three remediation steps. Use stonewright-elementor-page-digest only if structure context is needed. Do not mutate the document unless I explicitly expand scope.
prompts.verification: Performance audit metrics returned; remediation list is actionable; no raw _elementor_data dump.

prompts.title: What can you do with my page builder?
prompts.summary: Report Elementor and third-party block-library capabilities available on this site.
prerequisites: At least one page builder or block library installed
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start, then stonewright-site-capabilities. Report whether Elementor, Gutenberg/FSE, GenerateBlocks, Kadence Blocks, Spectra, or Blocksy is active, and for Elementor whether its own MCP module is available (native_elementor). When Elementor is present, call stonewright-elementor-v3-status. When a third-party block library is active, call stonewright-blocks-library-check-setup, and stonewright-blocks-library-list-blocks for GenerateBlocks, Kadence Blocks, or Spectra. Summarize what I can build natively on this site without inventing widgets or block attributes.
prompts.verification: Active builders/libraries listed with version signals; no invented widget or block schemas.

prompts.title: Custom code with human approval
prompts.summary: Prepare an exact theme-file or Customizer CSS proposal and stop for a human-issued one-time grant.
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright and call stonewright-task-start first. Prove the native gap, then run the matching approval-gated custom-code tool with dry_run:true. Return approval_url, exact path, before_bytes, after_bytes, changed_bytes, and a short change summary, then stop. Do not open the approval page, issue or retrieve the grant, or apply the candidate unless I explicitly ask you to perform that approval step. After I send the one-time custom_code_grant, apply only the exact approved hash and report backup, readback, the health check, rollback status, and the change_set id.
prompts.verification: No write occurs before the human-issued grant; candidate path and hash remain unchanged; apply reports verified readback, the health check result, and audit fields.

prompts.title: Make a change with Rescue watching
prompts.summary: Write through a typed ability, read the health check, and never call the site healthy without evidence.
prerequisites: The site can call itself over HTTP, or the change stays marked not verified
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start, then make this change only through a typed ability, never stonewright-php-execute: {{change}}. Stonewright records how to undo it first and asks the site whether it still loads afterwards. Report the change_set verification and any Rescue outcome (stonewright_rescue_write_rolled_back or stonewright_rescue_rollback_failed, with site_status). If a notice says the health check is unavailable, tell me the change is not verified and check the page and wp-admin another way. If a response carries pending_incident, stop and call stonewright-rescue-status before any other write. Do not retry a rolled-back change without changing the approach.
prompts.verification: Result says verified, rolled back, or not verified, with evidence; no healthy claim without a passing check; no retry before the incident is closed.

prompts.title: Roll back a failed change
prompts.summary: Undo a change that left the site failing: dry run first, then confirm the site loads.
prerequisites: An open incident or a change that was armed and never verified
prompts.prompt: Use Stonewright. Call stonewright-task-start, then stonewright-rescue-status. For the open incident, call stonewright-rescue-rollback with its incident_id and dry_run:true, and tell me what it restores, how old the change is, and any warning that a newer change to the same item would be overwritten. Wait for my yes. In production-safe mode get a one-use confirmation token from stonewright-security-issue-confirmation-token for exactly the call that follows. Then run the rollback and check that site_status is healthy. If a person already undid the change by hand, use action recheck instead. Do not undo it with stonewright-php-execute or WP-CLI. If the site does not load at all, tell me to use Stonewright > Rescue, the rescue link in the WordPress recovery mode email, or wp stonewright rescue status.
prompts.verification: site_status is healthy after the rollback; the outcome is on the change set and in Stonewright > Audit log; no write ran before my confirmation.
